items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1969-05-30
items.q: I had this little kid with me like I said, little Papu, Walter Nelson. It was we four... I want this band... I'm going to name y'all the Four Hairs Combo.

ctx.x: And you think back, they were calling you Professor Longhand when I used to follow him.

No, let me tell you when they started calling me Professor Longhand. We were down here at the Caledonia Inn playing Bixley, me, and Eight Man Black was on saxophone. And I just remember who all, well I had this little kid with me like I said, little Papu, Walter Nelson. It was we four. I had long hair then. Slick had, his hair was long but it wasn't quite as long as mine then. My hair was as long as you. All of that, then I was wearing that then. Them days was against the law. Anyway, by me teaching these fellas,…

Did you ever know any country blues players? Any pickers or anything like that? Any bottleneck players? Like I said, I met a lot of them. Chad Atkins. I don't know whether you call him a country man. I hear. He's good, man. He's a really good guitar player.

items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1975-11-13
items.q: What about, wouldn't Walter Nelson with you? [INTERVIEWER] Not at that time.

ctx.x: Yeah, this is just amateur stuff.

Yeah. To make a quarter, you know. First group that I formed was Al Miller. With Al Miller. Yeah. Robert Parker. One size. One that recorded Balfootin'. Yeah. And myself. It was hard to go way back. I had another kid with me with a- Swish? No, this was a different thing. This was the very first group that I formed. And I came to, I can't think of his name, but he was a little, he certainly looked like a little Hungarian boy. He wasn't from here, you know. What about, wouldn't Walter Nelson with you?
